transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-28
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Murphy (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Head of ML, CalmCare), Marcus Lee (CTO), Dana Ortiz (DevOps), Evan Brooks (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick model catalog walkthrough focused on selecting open models for CalmCare's clinical summarization use case. Discussed benchmarks (latency/cost/quality), platform compatibility (GGUF, AWQ, Triton), and deployment choices (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC). Agreed next steps for POC and benchmarks.

Topics: Model Catalog, Benchmarks, Compatibility Matrix, Quantization, VPC/Private deployment, Security docs, POC next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. um, we have about 50 minutes, i'll do a quick intro and then Samir will walk through the model catalog and some benchmark results. Priya, Marcus, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Priya: yep thanks Alex. sidelong hi from our side — Marcus is on, dana and evan too. we mostly want to understand model choices for clinical summarization and what tradeoffs look like.
[00:23] Alex: perfect. quick background — Redwood's model catalog is a curated list of open models and variants, we show perf profiles, compatibility (gguf, awq, fp16), and recommended quantization for latency/cost balance. We also surface redwood optimize suggestions for batching and caching.
[00:40] Samir: ok i'll share my screen — uh sorry if the screen names come through weird. so here's the catalog view, top line we have family names, then variants — e.g., LlamaX-2-13b (weirdly sometimes spelled in our internal notes), Mistral-7B, Redwoo-2-mini (note: my notes have typos). you can filter by task, latency target, and compat formats.
[01:05] Marcus: quick q — our infra team cares about model formats. we plan to run on-prem for PHI-sensitive records. does catalog show which models are available as gguf or gguf+awq?
[01:16] Samir: yes, compatibility matrix per model — formats (gguf, ggml, awq, fp16 gguf), and supported runtimes (Redwood runtime, Tritron, torchserve — sometimes we see the name tritron in docs mistakenly). we flag models that have verified perf on our Dedicated pools vs only on Hosted.
[01:35] Dana: do you have examples of latency numbers at 1k token responses? our users need < 800 ms P95 ideally.
[01:44] Samir: we ran microbenchmarks — caveat: this is on our 4xA100 Dedicated pools. examples: Mistral-7B int8 awq ~ 120 ms per 1-token step, end-to-end for 1k tokens ~ 420 ms median, P95 around 720 ms with batching disabled. LlamaX-2-13b fp16 ~ 650 ms median and P95 ~1.1s. These are approximate; we'll run with your sample data to validate.
[02:10] Priya: mhm, those numbers are helpful. how about quality tradeoff with awq/int8 — we care about clinical accuracy and hallucination reduction.
[02:22] Samir: great question. in the catalog we include benchmark tags: Rouge/ROUGE-like and a custom clinical F1 on our evaluation sets. AWQ/int8 sometimes has a small drop in NLG metrics — like 1–3% on our clinical prompts — but can be negligible with per-run QA and selected quant configs. we also offer hybrid modes: K-V cache in fp16 while attention runs int8 to preserve output fidelity.
[02:44] Evan: security question — if we go private on-prem, what about key management and audit logs? we need KMS/HSM and detailed audit trails.
[02:54] Alex: for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, and centralized audit logs which feed into your SIEM. we have SOC 2 docs and a checklist — i'll send the security pack.
[03:06] Evan: perfect. can you confirm data residency options? some of our records must remain in us-east-1.
[03:12] Alex: yes, you can pin deployments to region or run in your VPC on-prem. Dedicated offers region pinning; Private is fully under your control.
[03:20] Speaker 2: (mumble) sorry, can you show the console where batching is configured?
[03:25] Samir: sure — here's the Redwood Console route config. you can set batching windows, max batch size, prefix cache TTLs. On the optimize tab we recommend config sets based on observed sequence length distribution — for CalmCare we'd set aggressive prefix caching for repeated templates.
[03:45] Priya: how does prefix caching interact with clinical PII data? we have to make sure we don't cache PHI.
[03:52] Samir: good catch — caching in Redwood can be scoped per-route and can be turned off. for PHI flows we'd disable prefix caching or encrypt cache with customer keys; the console shows an option to exclude specific routes from K-V cache.
[04:10] Marcus: what about throughput — we have spikes during daily digest generation, need throughput of ~600 reqs/min with median 400 tokens per response.
[04:20] Samir: for throughput we recommend Dedicated with autoscale pools and burst capacity. the model catalog annotates throughput per GPU for each model/format — e.g., Mistral-7B int8 on an A100 ~ 80 reqs/min for 512-token avg; LlamaX-13b fp16 ~ 25 reqs/min. you'll want a mix: hosted for low-latency realtime and Dedicated for batch digests.
[04:45] Priya: is there an easy way to compare models side-by-side? like a compatibility+perf matrix we can export?
[04:50] Samir: yes, the UI has export CSV for the compatibility matrix and benchmark sheet; i'll attach the sheet but we'll also run the microbenchmarks with your dataset.
[04:59] Alex: to set expectations — hosted is fastest to integrate and has our open model fleet with SLAs for premium tiers; Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolation, Private gives full control but needs more ops effort.
[05:12] Dana: ops question — what does the deploy pipeline look like for Private? we use k8s and argo workflows.
[05:18] Samir: Private installs as a helm chart with an operator. We integrate with your k8s and can use argo for rollouts. we also have an on-prem bundle if you want air-gapped. note: some customers see slight perf differences due to local kernel and CUDA versions, so we recommend the same driver matrix we publish in the docs.
[05:40] Marcus: about cost — can you show cost delta between fp16 and int8?
[05:45] Samir: rough math: int8 AWQ gives ~2.5–3x token cost reduction vs fp16 on our billing model. the catalog has unit token cost estimates per model+quant. we'll run your sample and share a modeled cost sheet.
[06:00] Priya: okay. next, can you talk about model safety and guardrails? healthcare needs hallucination controls and redaction.
[06:08] Alex: Redwood supports function/tool calling to constrain outputs, and we have post-processing hooks to run hallucination detectors and redaction before returning to client. We can also integrate your internal classifiers.
[06:22] Evan: we need to review retention and logs — how long are verbatim requests stored?
[06:28] Alex: default retention on Hosted is 30 days for inference logs, but on Dedicated/Private you control retention policies. we can turn off verbatim logging or mask PII at ingestion.
[06:38] Priya: great. can you run a quick live example on catalog-selected model? maybe a short summarization on a canned patient note?
[06:45] Samir: yeah i'll paste a small note and run it through Mistral-7B int8 and then LlamaX-13B fp16 to show differences — bear with me while i switch context.
[07:10] [07:10] Samir: ok results are up — Mistral int8 summary: "Patient with hx of HTN presented with chest pain, underwent EKG, troponin negative, discharged with plan for outpatient cardiology f/u." LlamaX-13B fp16 summary: "Middle-aged patient, history of hypertension, chest pain evaluation negative for MI; recommended outpatient cardiology and modify HTN meds."
[07:35] Priya: looks similar; any hallucinations?
[07:37] Samir: none obvious here but in longer notes fp16 tends to keep more nuanced context — again we can tune prompt templates and use retrieval augmentation to reduce hallucinations.
[07:50] Marcus: i'd like the exported csv and the benchmark sheet.
[07:53] Alex: will send. also Samir, we should note the runtime configs you used.
[07:58] Samir: notes: Dedicated 4xA100, batch size 1 for latency test, int8 AWQ with per-layer quant config, tokens truncated at 1k. I'll include the exact command and triton-ish flags in the spreadsheet.
[08:18] Priya: about POC — we want a 2-week pilot to validate latency and quality on our corpus. can Redwood support that?
[08:24] Alex: yes we typically do a 2-week POC: Redwood SE runs benchmarks and helps configure Dedicated or Private. we'll propose scope in the next email.
[08:32] Evan: also need security touchpoint — a short call with Redwood security to run through SOC 2, encryption at rest, KMS, and log access.
[08:40] Alex: noted. Evan, we'll schedule a security review early next week. I'll include our SOC2 and the checklist.
[08:48] Priya: timeline wise, we hope to start pilot by Jan 9. is that realistic?
[08:53] Alex: yes if we get sample data and access by Jan 4, SE can run microbenchmarks and we can kickoff Jan 9.
[08:59] Speaker 1: (crosstalk) cool
[09:02] Samir: closing notes — i'll attach the model compatibility matrix CSV, the microbenchmark sheet, and a sample config. Alex will send pricing and contract.
[09:12] Alex: thanks everyone. recap: 1) Alex send pricing, model catalog and SOC2 pack; 2) Samir run bench with sample data; 3) Priya provide prompts & S3; 4) schedule POC kickoff week of Jan 9; 5) security review with Evan.
[09:30] Priya: thanks all, look forward to the spreadsheet.
[09:34] Marcus: thanks. bye.

Notes: Minor transcription artifacts: "Redwoo" and "Tritron" appear in transcript, some speaker labels as Speaker 1/2. References: Model catalog UI export link (shared in chat), benchmark spreadsheet link (sheet.redwood.example/benchmark-calmcare) — links to be attached to follow-up email.
